observed_pass.perimeter: The north weathered gray-tile/white-plaster wall, side runs, south gate wall and buildings now read as one bounded estate rather than isolated props or six floating patches.
observed_pass.main_hall_joins: Both north terminal wall segments disappear under the main-hall eaves and meet the structural plinth without a visible 40px-class gap or covering the facade door/windows.
observed_pass.south_gate_joins: The added foreground stone-base connectors close the measured west/east jamb gaps. Their natural depth does not create a floating strip and the central gate opening remains visually unobstructed.
observed_pass.openings: The central gate and both four-column open corridor bays remain legible intentional passages; the art does not suggest they were sealed by hidden collision.
observed_pass.peony_beds: Both cleaned peony beds have coherent adult-scale stone bases, retain flower detail, sit symmetrically outside the gate and leave the central approach clear.
observed_pass.material_family: The former blue-gray panel/dash-strip horizontal walls are absent. Horizontal enclosure surfaces now share the existing courtyard gate's aged plaster, exposed brick, dark plinth and gray tile family.

approved_scope.meaning: The current estate visual assembly may proceed through the already planned formal source binding, real movement, gate/corridor traversal and room-return validation. This admission is not a request for another art iteration.

known_limits: The two long side-wall runs use simplified low-detail longitudinal gray roof modules; at this small scale they are serviceable boundary depth, but remain less weathered and less detailed than the hall/gate artwork.
The courtyard retains strongly repeated paving and mirrored side components; it is a finished playable estate assembly for this scope, not a claim of unique hand-authored detail in every tile.

This native image contains no player/NPC and does not itself prove Field lighting, save state, route execution, doorway return, whole-city art quality or historical reconstruction. Those require the separate runtime checks already owned by Root/System.
